provenance.note: 2026-09-27: the reference nozzle these constants were fitted with (K 2.8, 100 bar, SMD 90 um) was back-figured, not published by SOLIT2, and has been withdrawn; the anchors now run only on a tester-supplied reference nozzle (designs/solit2-reference-nozzle.json). The ceiling correlation is now the published one (1.0, no longer fitted) and the droplet spread is each nozzle's measured Dv50/Dv90. Every fitted constant below therefore carries an assumed nozzle and a superseded 0.314 ceiling multiplier until refit against a tester-supplied reference nozzle (uv run python -m validation.fit --reference-nozzle PATH --max-nfev N). Earlier record: A least-squares fit of the constants in validation/fit.py FITTED_KEYS against reference cases c4-c6 has been run; every other constant here is hand-set from published literature and is not a fitted value. FITTED IS NOT VALIDATED: `solit2 validate` exits non-zero and lists every miss. Last refit 2026-09-23, after the anchors were corrected to their own Annex 2 figures (c4/c5 fire growth start, c6 activation and velocity, c5 measured peak): 12 of 19 comparisons pass and no constant rests on a bound. Peak heat release is inside tolerance on c4 and c6 but 1.7x high on c5 (26.6 MW against 15.5 measured). Gas temperature is 2-4x low: peak ceiling 201 C against 830 on c4 and 227 C against 580 on c5, because thermal.ceiling_excess_coefficient sits at 0.31 of the published Li & Ingason correlation. That multiplier is not a physical parameter, and the fit can only warm the gas by growing the fire, which is why it accepts c5's peak high. Before the anchor corrections, removing the multiplier put all six temperature comparisons inside tolerance while suppressed heat release on c4 jumped to 67 MW against 30, because the assumed spray evaporates before it lands once the gas is at its real temperature; that has not been re-measured since. See docs/accuracy-roadmap.md item 3; do not settle it by choosing a multiplier. c6's pools go out by flame cooling, an upper-bound criterion; pool_burning_rate_reduction and pool_extinction_flux_mm_min did not move in the fit because almost no water reaches the pools. All three reference cases rest on an ASSUMED nozzle specification, because SOLIT2 Annex 2 publishes the application density but neither the K-factor nor the droplet spectrum, so these constants have absorbed that assumption and do not transfer to a different nozzle without new test data. `anchor` names the reference cases a constant was set against; it must name only cases that still exist in validation/anchors, or "none".
provenance.reference_cases: SOLIT2 Engineering Guidance Annex 2, full-scale fire tests c4 (Class A with cover), c5 (Class A without cover) and c6 (Class B diesel pools).

pool_ramp_s.note: Annex 2: pools need 2-3 min to develop

pool_extinction_time_s.note: per pool; Annex 2: extinguished pool by pool

critical_velocity_height.note: H in Li-Ingason; mean height gives ~5% lower u_c

flame_length_coefficient.note: SET BY CONSTRAINT, NOT BY THE FIT. C_f, the horizontal reach of flame that cannot rise into the headroom: tip = C_f * max(flame_length - flame_clearance, 0). Was 4.3 carrying a citation (Ingason & Li, Tunnel Fire Dynamics ch.11) that cannot be verified against anything in this repo, and at that value it projected 89 m of flame downstream from a 10 m mock-up at 150 MW, putting the Annex 7 5.2.6 target in flame contact above about 12 MW and making the section 7.2.1 criterion read IGNITED in every configuration. target_ignited is a boolean, so its residual is a step function of this constant and least_squares sees exactly zero gradient -- a run with it in FITTED_KEYS left it at 4.3 untouched. Bisection against the c4 measured outcome gives the binding limit: the c4 target stays safe only below 1.1666 (c5 below 2.6305). 1.0 sits under that with margin and is the volume-conserving reading -- deflected flame length equals the vertical excess, 1:1 -- which is the defensible default in the absence of a checkable source.

ceiling_excess_coefficient.note: SET, NOT FITTED: the published Li & Ingason (2012) maximum ceiling excess, unscaled. Was 0.314, pinned at the fit's 0.3 floor, because the same scaled excess is the gas the mist droplets fall through: the fit bought correct suppressed heat release with gas temperatures 3x below SOLIT2 Annex 2 (c4 201 C vs 830 C). Removed from validation/fit.py FITTED_KEYS on 2026-09-27; see docs/accuracy-roadmap.md item 3.

eta_max.note: SOLIT2 held a 150 MW potential load to ~30 MW, so the ceiling is at least 0.80

w_ref_mm_min.note: basis removed with c1-c3; refit required. Was set against reference cases c1, c2 and c3, none of which survive in validation/anchors, so this value currently rests on nothing and is carried unchanged only to avoid silently altering the physics. Its MEANING is unchanged by the hardening exponent below, which is 1 at the moment discharge starts: this is still the water number that buys 1-1/e of eta_max against a fully involved, unsuppressed fire.

suppression_hardening_exponent.note: SET BY CONSTRAINT, NOT BY THE FIT, and 0.0 switches the term off. p in eta = eta_max * (1 - exp(-(w_fuel * f_cov / w_ref) * f_burn ** p)), where f_burn = hrr / hrr_free is the share of the free-burning fire still alive. p > 0 says the residual fire is the hard part: the exposed fuel the spray can reach burns away or is wetted first and what is left is the shielded, deep-seated load, so each further increment of knockdown costs disproportionately more water. That is what SOLIT2 Annex 2 6.1 and 6.2 report -- the HRR 'was limited to a significantly lower level' for the full 30 minutes of discharge and the brigade still had to 'finally extinguish the remaining fire'. Held off the evaporation cliff the term does exactly what it should: at p=0.5 c4 settles at 32.6 MW within a 2.4% band and the level falls monotonically with water (630/840/1260/1680 lpm -> 47.2/32.6/19.0/13.8 MW). It CANNOT be switched on in this engine. w_fuel falls 109x between 275 K and 350 K of ceiling excess and is flat at 0.013 mm/min above that; a 30 MW plateau sits at ~200 K on the shoulder of that cliff, so any p >= 0.10 lifts c4 over it and the fire escapes to ~144 MW (p=0.05 -> peak 38.3 MW, p=0.10 -> 143.1 MW). 0.0 is the only value that does not make c4 and c5 worse, and it reproduces the previous law exactly. DELIBERATELY NOT IN FITTED_KEYS: the peak-HRR residual is a step in p and not a continuous function of it, and least_squares' relative DIFF_STEP is identically zero at p=0 in any case. Raise it only once the delivery stops being near-binary in gas temperature -- evaporation_k_ref_m2s is already resting on its lower bound, so the fit cannot move the cliff.

evaporation_k_ref_m2s.note: basis removed with c3; refit required. d-squared law constant at the reference gas temperature rise; a 100 um drop evaporates in ~0.1 s at that rise and essentially not at all in cool air. The magnitude is physically reasonable but the specific value was set against c3, which no longer exists.

evaporation_reference_delta_t_k.note: basis removed with c3; refit required. Paired with evaporation_k_ref_m2s and set against the same deleted reference case.

flank_reach_factor.note: lateral band, as a multiple of fuel height, in which descending spray strikes the fuel's sides

flank_efficiency.note: effectiveness of water striking a vertical face relative to water landing on the top face

shielding_reference_loading_kgm3.note: water mass loading at which the droplet's local environment departs materially from the ambient plume; below it a droplet is effectively alone, above it the spray core is partly self-shielded. The starting value and the fitted bounds are an order-of-magnitude engineering guess, NOT a literature figure.

shielding_floor.note: minimum shield factor at very high loading; the spray still entrains hot ambient gas so full insulation from it is not physical. Deliberately NOT fitted: it is a fixed modelling assumption, and adding it to the search space would grow it past what a twenty-minute budget can usefully explore for a constant this unlikely to be identifiable on its own.
